Network Centrality Reveals Dissociable Brain Activity during
Response Inhibition in Human Right Ventral Part of Inferior Frontal Cortex

Abstract—The human right inferior frontal cortex (IFC) plays a critical role in response inhibition. It has also been
demonstrated that the IFC is heterogeneous and that the ventral part of the IFC (vIFC) is more critical to inhibition
of prepotent response tendency. Recent areal parcellation analyses based on resting-state functional connectiv-
ity have revealed that the right vIFC consists of multiple functional areas. In the present study, we characterized
the parcellated areas (parcels) in the right vIFC using graph theory analysis, which characterizes local connectiv-
ity properties of a brain network by referring to its global structure of functional connectivity. Functional magnetic
resonance imaging (MRI) scans were obtained during performance of a stop-signal task and during resting state.
The cerebral cortex was parcellated into areas using resting-state functional connectivity. The parcels were then
subjected to graph theory analysis to reveal central areas. Two parcels, ventral and dorsal, in the posterior part of
the vIFC, exhibited signiﬁcant brain activity during response inhibition. The ventral parcel exhibited a positive
correlation between betweenness centrality and brain activity while the dorsal parcel did not. Correlations were
signiﬁcantly stronger in the ventral parcel. Moreover, the ventral parcel exhibited a negative correlation between
brain activity during response inhibition and stop-signal reaction time (SSRT), a behavioral measure used to eval-
uate stopping performance. These dissociation results suggest that the ventral region in the vIFC plays a more
central role in the brain network by increasing brain activity, which may further predict better performance of
response inhibition. (cid:1) 2020 IBRO. Published by Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved.
Key words: Boundary mapping, Inferior frontal gyrus, Inferior frontal junction.

DISCUSSION
In the present fMRI study, the
cerebral cortex was parcellated
into functional areas, and the
centrality indices of the graph
theory and the brain activity
during response inhibition were
calculated on an ROI basis. The
two ROIs along the precentral
sulcus in the right vIFC were
activated during response
inhibition. The correlation between
centrality and brain activity was
signiﬁcant in ROI 1 (located more
ventrally), whereas the correlation
in ROI 2 (located more dorsally)
was not signiﬁcant. The diﬀerence
of the correlations was signiﬁcant.
In ROI 1, the correlation between
brain activity and SSRT was also
signiﬁcant. These results
demonstrate the dissociation in
the right vIFC in terms of the
network centrality and suggest
that the ventral parcel plays a
central role in the brain network
that increases brain activity in the
parcel, which may further predict
better performance of response
inhibition.

The parcellation analyses based on boundary

et al., 2017, 2019; Ogawa et al., 2018 ) were applied to
the cerebral cortical surface. Mean gray matter signalwas regressed out, followed by
spatial smoothing (FWHM =
6 mm). Each vertex in the corticalsurface of each subject was usedas a seed to calculate its correla-
tions with all the vertices. Spatial
pattern similarity of the correlationmaps was evaluated using correla-
tion coeﬃcients, and similarity
maps were generated. Spatial gra-dients of the similarity maps were
computed for each seed vertex,
and the gradient maps of individualsubjects were averaged across the
subjects. After spatial smoothing
(FWHM = 6 mm), a two-dimen-sional watershed algorithm wasapplied to the gradient maps, and
the binary watershed maps were
averaged across seed vertices togenerate a boundary probability
map. The watershed algorithm
was again applied to the boundaryprobability map to delineate parcel-
lated regions.
For subsequent analyses, to
avoid non-uniform signal to noiseratio caused by the diﬀerent
number of vertices in the parcels,
we deﬁned regions of interest(ROIs) of 40 vertices closest to
the centroid of each parcel. When
a parcel contained less than 40vertices, the ROI included all the
vertices in the parcel.


Network construction and
centrality calculation
Correlation coeﬃcients of prepro-
cessed time-series of functional
images were calculated as themagnitude values of functional
connectivity between the parcels.
The correlation coeﬃcientsbetween the parcels weretransformed to zvalues using
Fisher transformation and then
normalized to the standard normaldistribution (average = 0 and
standard deviation = 1). Nodes of
the network represented the parcels, and edgesrepresented the connectivity. To deﬁne a binary
undirected network for each subject, a proportional

In total, 377 parcels (192 in left hemisphere and 185 in
right hemisphere) were identiﬁed in the cortical surfaces
(Fig. 2 A). ROIs consisted of 40 vertices closest to the
centroid ( Fig. 2 B). For the 57 parcels that contained
less than 40 vertices, the ROI included all the vertices in
the parcel. The mean number of vertices in one ROI ofa parcel was 38.8 ± 3.7 (mean ± SD).
Centrality index
Correlation between parcels were calculated on the basis
of ROIs in the cortical parcels. The correlation matrix ofboth hemispheres was calculated and was binarized togenerate the adjacency matrix. Fig. 3 shows the
centrality index in the whole brain averaged across the
subjects. Parcels with high central index were observedin the supramarginal gyrus, anterior temporal cortex and
precuneus.
